added_claims.claim: The 2025 gold rally cannot be explained by inflation, which is lower than two years earlier, so central-bank reserve diversification away from traditional safe assets is the better explanation than inflation hedging or speculation.
added_claims.testable: partly - compare gold with inflation and central-bank purchases

added_claims.quote: why some people say gold is going up is for example the uncertainty about you know Fed independence

added_claims.quote: they get paid interest on their reserves that they hold in the Fed
added_claims.claim: With ample reserves and interest paid on reserves, banks no longer need to borrow reserves, so the Fed funds market has shrunk to foreign-bank buyers and Federal Home Loan Bank providers and no longer represents true money-market funding rates.

added_claims.testable: yes - volumes and rates are observable

added_claims.claim: In Denmark almost half of TV advertising is now from betting firms, an anecdotal gauge of how widespread retail speculation and betting products have become, which adds noise to markets.

added_claims.claim: Lending against inventory carries a double-pledging risk: the same collateral may back several loans, so lenders must verify inventory physically (windshield wipers in First Brands' warehouses).

added_claims.claim: Niels dislikes brokers publicising estimated CTA flows despite Chinese walls, because it exposes CTA positioning and creates conflict-of-interest and crowding risk for the managers who trade through them.

added_claims.claim: Current CTA practice relies on correlation, hierarchical clustering or PCA across markets and cointegration tests to decide which markets to hold, which treats connectedness only as a diversification input, not a causal or predictive one.

corrections.issue: Wrong chronology: central-bank selling coincided with the fall of gold to about 500 after the 1970s peak (the 1990s sales Mark mentioned), not with the decline after 2011; Niels's price levels (600 to 3,500, 2,500-2,600 at the GFC) are loosely recalled and do not match nominal prices.
corrections.fix: Niels notes three gold rallies (1978-80, GFC to about 2011, and now); after the 1970s surge prices fell sharply to roughly 500, around the time central banks were selling gold, and after the GFC-era peak they fell again less dramatically; his price levels are approximate or recalled loosely.
